Note::is_bytes¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

bool Note::is_bytes() const noexcept

Test Whether The Note Is In Bytes Mode¶

is_bytes() reports whether the complete Note has the NoteDType::Bytes dtype. Dtype belongs to the Note as a whole, so this is a scalar metadata query rather than an elementwise predicate. It returns true for raw-byte storage and false for Text, Bool, Int64, Float64, and undefined Notes.

Use it to branch before calling text-only methods (character length, case mapping, regex) that require a UTF-8-mode Note, or to assert that a pipeline stage produced the encoding you expected.

The query does not inspect or validate cell content. A Bytes Note may happen to contain valid UTF-8, while a Text Note carries text intent independently of a particular cell’s bytes. Use is_utf8_valid() when the question is whether each stored byte sequence is valid UTF-8.

The call is constant time, performs no allocation, and is safe on an undefined Note, for which it returns false.

Example 1: A UTF-8-Mode Note¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c"});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << n.is_bytes() << '\n';

Output¶

false

Example 2: A Bytes-Mode Note¶

const auto n = pluss::note::bytes({"a", "b"});
std::cout << std::boolalpha << n.is_bytes() << '\n';

Output¶

true

Example 3: Valid UTF-8 Does Not Change The Dtype¶

const auto raw = pluss::note::bytes({"plain ASCII", "caf\xC3\xA9"});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "bytes: " << raw.is_bytes() << '\n'
          << "valid: ";
const auto valid = raw.is_utf8_valid();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < valid.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? " " : "") << static_cast<int>(valid[i]);
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

bytes: true
valid: 1 1

Both cells decode as UTF-8, but the Note remains Bytes until an explicit conversion such as to_utf8_strict() produces a Text Note.

Failure Behavior¶

is_bytes() has no failure path. It reads only the dtype tag and does not dereference cell storage. In particular, Note::undefined().is_bytes() is false; use defined() separately when absence must be distinguished from a defined non-Bytes Note.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::bytes: build a bytes-mode Note.

  • Note::is_utf8_valid: whether the bytes would decode cleanly as UTF-8.

  • pluss::coden::Note::to_utf8_lossy: switch a bytes-mode Note to text.
